intro: 50 ADHD topics with a strong chance of spreading on LinkedIn: specific, relatable, slightly contrarian, and easy to tell as a story. A fresh set is written on the 1st of every month, and no hook from a previous month is reused.
note: First-person prompts assume lived experience. If it isn't yours, frame it as what you've heard from users (with permission), or pick another prompt. No medical claims and no invented numbers: fill [placeholders] with real ones.

prompts.hook: Year-end reviews ask ADHD brains to remember 12 months. Most of us barely remember Tuesday.
prompts.prompt: Write about performance-review season and the running “wins doc” habit that saves you from blanking.

prompts.hook: Q4 deadlines don't create urgency for me. They create paralysis.
prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between pressure that activates you and pressure that freezes you, and how you split one big Q4 goal into a first step.

prompts.hook: The best workplace accommodation I ever got cost my company nothing.
prompts.prompt: Share one specific, low-cost adjustment (written follow-ups, a quiet hour, a flexible start) and why it worked. Only if it's real.

prompts.hook: New research on neurodivergence at work. Here's what managers should actually take from it.
prompts.prompt: Screenshot a recent study's headline (for example NDSU's September 2026 workplace research), summarise it accurately, and add your own practical takeaway without overstating the findings.

prompts.hook: I write my meeting notes before the meeting.
prompts.prompt: Explain how drafting the agenda and the decision you need ahead of time keeps an ADHD brain on track, with a before/after example.

prompts.hook: Companies are publishing ADHD guides. Most miss the one thing that matters.
prompts.prompt: React to the new wave of employer ADHD guidance: what it gets right, and the one thing you'd add (asking the person what helps them).

prompts.hook: My calendar has buffer blocks and I'll defend them in any meeting.
prompts.prompt: Show a redacted week with transition buffers and explain why switching costs more than the meetings themselves.

prompts.hook: The hardest part of my job isn't the work. It's switching between kinds of work.
prompts.prompt: Write about task-switching and the batching habit that gave you back an afternoon.

prompts.hook: “I'll get back to you” is a promise my brain can't keep track of.
prompts.prompt: Share the capture habit that turns every “I'll get back to you” into something you actually follow up on.

prompts.hook: 4 things that make a job description ADHD-friendly (without ever saying ADHD).
prompts.prompt: One idea per slide: clear outcomes over vague duties, written processes, flexible hours, async options.

prompts.hook: ADHD at work isn't a superpower or a disability. It's a fit problem.
prompts.prompt: Make the case for “mismatch” as the useful frame, with one role that fit and one that didn't.

prompts.hook: More ADHD diagnoses doesn't mean ADHD is a trend.
prompts.prompt: Write a balanced take on the debate sparked by the UK government-commissioned review published in October 2026 (assessment quality, rising diagnoses, long waits). Cite it, and make no clinical claims.

prompts.hook: “You don't look like you have ADHD.” What does it look like, then?
prompts.prompt: Write a calm, slightly witty reply to the line many adults hear, and say what's usually invisible.

prompts.hook: Running late isn't disrespect. Here's what's actually going on.
prompts.prompt: Explain the gap between intending to be on time and being on time, and what helps.

prompts.hook: For ADHD brains, interest is the fuel. Importance isn't.
prompts.prompt: Unpack the “interest-based” idea (credit the clinicians who popularised it) with an everyday example.

prompts.hook: Unfinished projects aren't failures. They're a map of what pulled me in.
prompts.prompt: Reframe the graveyard of half-done projects, and say which one deserves to be finished.

prompts.hook: Organisation tips assume you'll remember to use them.
prompts.prompt: Point out the hidden step in most productivity advice and what to do about it.

prompts.hook: Many adults don't grow out of ADHD. They grow around it.
prompts.prompt: Write about the workarounds people quietly build over the years, and which ones are worth teaching earlier.

prompts.hook: What people get wrong about ADHD and boredom.
prompts.prompt: Explain why boredom feels unbearable rather than mildly annoying, using a real moment, without medical claims.

prompts.hook: Accommodations aren't special treatment. They're removing friction.
prompts.prompt: Five everyday examples, one per slide, that help everyone on a team.

prompts.hook: Diwali deep-clean with ADHD: [N] open projects and one very clean drawer.
prompts.prompt: A light, honest post about festival cleaning, hyperfocus on the wrong cupboard, and what you actually finished.

prompts.hook: The hardest day for my routine is the day after a holiday.
prompts.prompt: Write about re-entry after a break and the smallest step that gets you going again.

prompts.hook: ADHD Awareness Month just ended. Here's who quietly held me up.
prompts.prompt: October's theme was “A Community of Support”. Thank the specific people (or kinds of people) who make it easier, and say what they actually do.

prompts.hook: I waited [N] months for an ADHD assessment. Here's what the wait was like.
prompts.prompt: Only if it's your story, or shared with permission: the limbo, what helped while waiting, and what you'd tell someone on a list now.

prompts.hook: The “easy” tasks are the ones that sit on my list for weeks.
prompts.prompt: Explain why two-minute tasks can be the hardest, using a real one.

prompts.hook: What “I'm fine, just busy” usually means for me.
prompts.prompt: Translate the polite phrase honestly and say what kind of check-in actually helps.

prompts.hook: My phone's screen-time report is a diary I never meant to write.
prompts.prompt: Share a redacted screenshot and what it told you about your week.

prompts.hook: I don't forget birthdays because I don't care.
prompts.prompt: Write about ADHD and relationships: the guilt, the misread intent, and the system that fixed it.

prompts.hook: The relief of finally having words for it.
prompts.prompt: Describe the moment language (a diagnosis, a post, a person) made years of experience make sense.

prompts.hook: Things my brain does brilliantly at 11pm and never at 11am.
prompts.prompt: A light, relatable list, ending with how you now protect your real peak hours.

prompts.hook: My “wins doc” is the file that saves my performance review.
prompts.prompt: Show the template (redacted) and how you add to it in 30 seconds a week.

prompts.hook: I outsource remembering, not thinking.
prompts.prompt: Explain which jobs you hand to tools and AI (capture, reminders, first drafts) and which stay yours.

prompts.hook: The tab limit that stopped my browser from eating my day.
prompts.prompt: Share a tab or app limit you actually use, and what changed after a week.

prompts.hook: I asked AI to plan my week. Here's what it got wrong about ADHD.
prompts.prompt: Run the test honestly, screenshot the plan, and show what you'd change for a real ADHD week.

prompts.hook: I set alarms for when to leave, not for when to arrive.
prompts.prompt: Explain the shift and why it beats “be there at 3”.

prompts.hook: The “one more thing” trap, and the exit ritual that beats it.
prompts.prompt: Describe the trap before leaving or stopping, and the small ritual that gets you out the door.

prompts.hook: Voice notes are my second brain.
prompts.prompt: Show how you capture ideas while walking, and how they turn into action later.

prompts.hook: A visible to-do list beats a smart one.
prompts.prompt: Photograph your paper list or whiteboard and explain why “out of sight, out of mind” is literal.

prompts.hook: My end-of-day shutdown ritual takes [N] minutes.
prompts.prompt: Lay out the steps as a simple visual: close loops, park thoughts, set tomorrow's first task.

prompts.hook: What an ADHD-friendly app should never do.
prompts.prompt: For builders: no guilt streaks, no shame copy, no notification floods. One rule per slide, with why.

prompts.hook: What ADHD Awareness Month taught us at Dopami.
prompts.prompt: Share real lessons from October's conversations and content: what resonated and what you'll do differently.

prompts.hook: We asked [N] people what “support” means to them. The answers surprised us.
prompts.prompt: Only if you ran it: one answer per slide, and what you're changing because of them.

prompts.hook: Why Dopami is built around people, not just AI.
prompts.prompt: Explain the thinking behind pairing AI with human presence (body doubling, Done Together).

prompts.hook: The long wait for an ADHD assessment is a design problem too.
prompts.prompt: Respond to the waiting-list conversation: what tools and communities can offer people while they wait, with no clinical claims.

prompts.hook: A day in the life of building an ADHD product.
prompts.prompt: Real moments from one day: calls, design reviews, the messy parts.

prompts.hook: The mistake we almost made in our first version.
prompts.prompt: Only if true: what you nearly built, who stopped you, and what you learned.

prompts.hook: What I look for when hiring for an ADHD-first product.
prompts.prompt: The traits and experiences that matter more than a perfect CV.

prompts.hook: Our design rule: never punish someone for coming back late.
prompts.prompt: Only if it's a real Dopami principle: why missed days shouldn't reset progress, and how you design for return.

prompts.hook: The question users ask us most, and our honest answer.
prompts.prompt: Share the most common question from users or the waitlist and answer it plainly.

prompts.hook: If you've ever opened an app to focus and lost an hour, I'd love to talk.
prompts.prompt: A warm user-research call-out: who you want to speak with, what you'll ask, and how to book.
